newsitem.title: UK: Options - Coffee volatility continues to climb.
newsitem.headline: Options - Coffee volatility continues to climb.

text.p: At-the-money implied coffee options volatility continued to climb this week but without a clear pattern in put or call activity.
July LIFFE coffee tumbled sharply this week to its lowest level since mid-May from last week's 20-month high while New York's July contract dropped off 20-year highs.
Despite losses that brought coffee prices back into familiar territory, volatilities jumped because the drop happened so quickly, traders said.
Volatility increases were most notable in July and September, which remains higher than November.

Implied at-the-money July volatilities were pegged near 66.5 percent, up from about 60 percent a week ago. But traders said some out-of-the-money options traded as high as 90 to 100 percent earlier this week. They said a few $2,500 calls changed hands at about 100 percent volatility.
At-the-money implied September volatilities jumped to 72 to 73 percent from 69 percent and November edged up to 61 percent from about 60 percent.

But traders said there was no clear pattern in put and call activity. Though trade remained brisk, they said interest was seen in puts and calls on both sides of the market, indicating that investors were split on which the way prices would head next.
In cocoa, options activity remained quiet despite a rash of fund and trade liquidation mixed with some fresh sales that helped push July down to nearly a five-week low.
Because of the lack of interest in cocoa options, implied at-the money volatilities fell, traders said.
Earlier in the week, July volatility was offered down to about 16 percent from 23 percent a week ago and has since, lingered close to that level, traders said.
September slipped to 24 percent from about 25 percent last week, they said.
